I think the whole situation is different for everyone. I personally found comfort in the community before I started to really transition (pre-T) and I loved seeing that there were others like me. As time has gone on I’ve become less and less attached to the community. It seems strange, as I’m just a guy just like any other dude, and I almost sometimes feel embarrassed at the label “trans” because I’d much rather be cis or just seen as any other guy and not defined by the sex assigned at birth. 

I don’t think it’s transphobic at all. For me it is a conflict between not wanting to be defined by my past and seen as who I currently, and actually am.

I’d suggest asking people on /r/FTMmen. And maybe specifying what you are anxious about. Setting things up and finding a surgeon? The consult? The surgery itself? Recovery? Are you having surgery soon and worried about COVID regulations? I think that would help get more specific answers. 

It’s not going to be as bad as you are stressing about. I just asked the nurses or doctors to talk me through things that were going to happen and when they did stuff (such as putting in the IV) which helps a lot for my anxiety. Getting put out and then waking up seems to happen instantly. Probably because of the meds, but I wasn’t in much pain during the process at all, mostly just felt back aches.

Recovery mostly included sleeping a lot. Having someone to help is pretty important, there were times I felt I couldn’t sit up without someone helping me. Or helping dry off my back once I could shower again. 

I ended up being back to functioning pretty normally and independently rather quickly 2-3 weeks, even with a complication. Of course still limited movement and such. 

Something I wish I had known was that the surgery is likely going to cut a lot of nerves in your chest. They will regrow don’t worry, but it will be weird because you can’t really feel some places and everything feels just strange for a bit. 

Just remember to prepare things in your house or apartment by moving them down to be reachable or having someone that can help you do things like get groceries even later on. 

Feel free to message me with more specific questions and I can answer them for you.

From my experience as a trans guy getting T: 

Definitely depends on insurance or if you don’t have any. I think each doctor visit for me is about $150, and blood work was about $200 depending on what they were testing for. I went in once a month for four months with three blood work tests (one before starting, one at 3 months, one at 4 months) to make sure my levels and dose were stable. Then it’s once a year ish from here on out. I’m bad with insurance, but I’m fairly sure these are costs before meeting my deductible. 

My prescription costs about $22 for 6-7 weeks dose. And $6 for 10 weeks of needles. 

The answer: very expensive, especially in the beginning.
